column1: # ---- 03-contracts/C5 ----
C5 carries the StateUpdate payload at version 1.0 from L5 to L0 and is the only backwards edge in the system.
C5 is written at the end of a tick and read at the top of the next, so everything in it is by construction at least one tick old when used.
The one-tick lag on C5 is explicit and priceable rather than hidden.
The C5 envelope adds isFinal, revisionOf, and effectiveFrom, the slot from which the state applies.
realisedPeak is carried per regime and is the epigraph floor for the next tick.
realisedPeakSlot records when the realised peak occurred and is diagnostically important.
periodStart and periodEnd are the accounting period bounds per regime, derived from the local calendar.
peakIsProvisional is true per regime while meter data is unfinal.
unsettledGapFrom is the earliest slot not yet settled, per regime.
headroomToPeakKw is the distance from realisedPeak to the level at which a new peak would be set, and is the continuous analogue of qualificationMarginHours.
peakCritical is true when headroomToPeakKw is inside the configured margin, or the horizon contains a slot whose CVaR peak belief exceeds realisedPeak.
peakCritical forces tier escalation and the protective bound.
peakCritical is written by Settlement and read by L2's PeakView and L3's escalation policy.
peakCritical and qualCritical are both computed by Settlement and never by the Planner, so the escalation trigger cannot be influenced by the thing it is meant to guard.
unsettledGapFrom is what makes the lag safe.

The Planner knows the realised peak is authoritative only up to unsettledGapFrom and treats the gap conservatively, using its own modelled POI trajectory as a provisional peak contribution rather than assuming the gap contained nothing.
annualEnergyKwh is accumulated in the qualification year.
annualPeakKw is the denominator of full-load hours.
fullLoadHours is annualEnergy divided by annualPeak.
hlzfPeakKw is the peak within HLZF windows only.
qualificationStatus is one of Qualified, AtRisk, Lost or NotApplicable, per applicable §19(2) path.
qualificationMarginHours is the distance to the threshold and drives qualCritical.
projectedYearEndFlh is a forward projection from the slow loop.
qualCritical is true within the configured margin and forces tier escalation and the protective bound.

The margin is carried and not just the status, because a binary qualified flag tells the engine nothing until the moment it is too late, whereas the margin lets the value function price the approach to the cliff continuously.
The delineation state carries month-to-date accumulators of the Abgrenzungsoption machinery, computed by Settlement Phase A from Z1 and Z2 alone.
Seven accumulators are carried and no others, because everything from (10) to (33) is a closed-form function of them.
mtdGridImport is (3), the gesamter Netzbezug, defaulting to zero.
mtdStorageCharge is (5), the Verbrauch im Stromspeicher, defaulting to zero.
mtdStorageDischarge is (6), the Erzeugung im Stromspeicher, defaulting to zero.
mtdSimultaneousGridCharge is (9), the sum of MIN[Z1NB¼; Z2V¼], defaulting to zero.
mtdStorageExport is (11), the sum of MIN[Z1NE¼; Z2E¼], defaulting to zero.
mtdDirectFeedInAwPos is (26), direct feed-in in AW>0 hours only, defaulting to zero.
mtdStorageExportAwPos is (29), storage feed-in in AW>0 hours only, defaulting to zero.

The derived delineation quantities are published for readability and for the escalation triggers, are recomputable from the seven accumulators, and are carried so that four layers do not each re-derive them.
pvShare is (10)/(5), the PV share of charging, and sets the route split.
awPositiveShare is (30), a ratio, so a late-month AW=0 export dilutes the whole month's (28).
saldierungsfaehig is (16), the grey route.
foerderfaehig is (32), the green route.
umlagebelasteterNetzbezug is (21), the base of EnfgLevies.
fremdtank is (12) and is expected to be zero.
monthStart and monthEnd are Europe/Berlin civil-calendar bounds derived via CivilCalendar.
slotsToMonthEnd is a coordinate of V_del, and the accumulators reset at monthEnd.
throughputBoundMet is true when charge throughput exceeds η_d·E_usable/(1−η_rt) so that (12) = 0 is arithmetically assured, and its conservative default is not assured.
delineationIsProvisional is true while the month's meter data is unfinal.
The delineation accumulators reset to zero at monthEnd and SOC does not.

The month-boundary discontinuity is in value and not in physics: the same kWh in the same battery is worth a different amount either side of the boundary because the aggregates its route ran through have vanished.
slotsToMonthEnd is what lets V_del price the approach to the month boundary continuously, and it is the delineation counterpart of qualificationMarginHours.
A commitment ledger entry carries an entryId, a kind of SpotPosition, ReserveAward or OpenOrder, and a status of Pending, Confirmed, Settled or Cancelled.
The Pending versus Confirmed distinction in the commitment ledger is load-bearing.
signedVolume in the commitment ledger is in the market frame.
For reserve awards the feasibilityRequirement carries the SOC corridor that must be maintained.
A Confirmed reserve award's feasibilityRequirement becomes a hard constraint in every degradation mode.
Pending ledger entries are exposure rather than obligation, and the Planner treats them probabilistically.
Realised P&L is decomposed into the same EconomicEffect enumeration used by Valuation, so planned and realised value are comparable term by term.
plannedByEffect records what Valuation expected.
unexplained is a mandatory bucket carrying the effect-level residual, the realised cash not attributable to any EconomicEffect.
unexplainedRatio is alerted above a threshold.
The unexplained bucket is not optional and must not be allowed to be silently absorbed elsewhere.
A rising unexplained ratio is the single best early warning that a term definition has drifted between Valuation and Settlement.

unexplained in §5 is the residual of the cash decomposition and unexplainedError in §6 is the residual of the error decomposition; they are never netted against one another and each has its own invariant.
The error decomposition is the mechanism that makes the system improvable rather than merely operable.
The gap between planned value and realised value splits into four attributable buckets.
optimalityGap is the value given up because the tier actually used was not Tier 1, and its fix lives in L3.
forecastError is the value lost because the world differed from the belief the plan was built on, and its fix lives in L1 and the scenario model.
modelError is the value lost because the valuation was wrong given the belief, and its fix lives in L2.
executionSlippage is the value lost between intent and fill, and its fix lives in the quoting policy.
The decomposition telescopes from the Tier-1 reference value and not from the value of the plan that was actually used.
Ĵ₁ is the Tier-1 objective on the tick's beliefs and is the anchor of the decomposition.
Ĵ is the used-tier objective on the same beliefs, A is the used plan re-scored on realised outturn, and R is the realised value from settled cash.
optimalityGap = Ĵ₁ − Ĵ.
forecastError = Ĵ − A.
modelError plus executionSlippage plus unexplainedError equals A − R.
A suboptimal tier lowers the planned value and the realised value, so it nets out of planned minus realised entirely.
Anchoring at Ĵ would leave optimalityGap with nowhere to live and would silently attribute optimiser weakness to forecast error.
planned in INV-S-03 means Ĵ₁.
When Tier 1 was the tier used, Ĵ₁ = Ĵ and the two anchors coincide.
plannedByEffect remains the used-tier value because that is what the cash decomposition must reconcile against, and both anchors are recorded.
Each error bucket is a counterfactual re-run, possible only because every layer is a pure function of a recorded input.
optimalityGap is computed by re-solving the tick at Tier 1 on the recorded C2 payload and taking the difference of objective values.
forecastError is computed by re-scoring the plan that was actually submitted against realised outturn, holding the plan fixed, which is the telescoping form.
Re-planning on realised data measures the value of perfect foresight, which is recorded separately as valueOfForesight and is also the perfect-foresight upper bound.
The telescoping forecast error and the value of perfect foresight must not be conflated: one is a link in the chain and the other is a bound.
modelError is computed by valuing the actual trajectory using Valuation's own term definitions and comparing with Settlement's independent accounting of the same trajectory.
A non-zero modelError means Valuation and Settlement disagree about what a MWh was worth, which is a definition drift.
executionSlippage is computed by valuing the fills at intent prices versus executed prices.
ActivationRisk and the CVaR weighting are objective penalties and not cashflows.
Realised value can never contain risk penalties, so comparing a risk-loaded planned value against a risk-free realised one books the risk premium as a loss every single day.
Both sides of the error decomposition use the risk-free objective.
PlanResult reports gross risk-free and net risk-loaded values, and only the gross figure enters the error decomposition chain.
The four error buckets plus unexplainedError sum to Ĵ₁ − R within tolerance.
The four-way error split is what turns a statement about losing money last week into a statement about the load forecast degrading on Tuesdays, which is actionable.
degradationMode is computed centrally and written in C5.
modeTransitions carries the full audit trail of (SlotId, from, to, cause) for the period.
ticksByMode lets P&L be conditioned on operating mode.
seriesQualitySummary feeds data-source SLAs.
vSocStale is true beyond the value function's validityHorizon.
stateDriftSignal measures how far the current state is from where V was fitted.
refreshRequested indicates the slow loop should re-run.
stateDriftSignal allows the slow loop to be event-driven rather than purely periodic, because a large peak event or a qualification status change invalidates V faster than the calendar does.
realisedPeak is non-decreasing within an accounting period and resets exactly at the local-calendar boundary, and violation is a HALT.
realisedByEffect sums, with unexplained, to total realised P&L, and violation is a HALT.
The four error buckets sum to planned minus realised within tolerance, and violation warns.
There is no reserve delivery shortfall, mirroring C4, and violation alerts and halts.
Every Confirmed commitment has a feasibilityRequirement where the product requires one, and violation is a HALT.
fullLoadHours equals annualEnergyKwh divided by annualPeakKw within tolerance, and violation is a HALT.
unexplainedRatio is below threshold, and violation warns, escalating to alert.
State is never written for a slot earlier than effectiveFrom of the previous update, except as an explicit revisionOf, and violation is a HALT.
